newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end down on Jinro, Chung Won troubles.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end down on Jinro, Chung Won troubles.

text.p: News of financial troubles at Jinro Ltd and Chung Won Corp sent South Korean stocks to a lower close on Tuesday, brokers said.
The composite index shed 9.38 points, or 1.35 percent, to close at 687.96.
Trading in both Jinro and Chung Won was suspended.
"Investors' sentiment quickly froze due to the default news and selling was across the board," said analyst Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Dealers said chipmakers fell on talks that memory chip prices were easing after having picked up early this year.

Brokers said the market's fall was halted towards the close as the bond market remained unmoved by the news. Bond market dealers said the benchmark three-year corporate bonds were trading flat at 12.43 percent.
A creditor bank official said on Tuesday Jinro Ltd, flagship unit of the troubled Jinro Group, on Monday defaulted on 50.4 billion won worth of promissory notes and cheques.
But the Commercial Bank of Korea official said all of Jinro Ltd's bank accounts would remain open under an earlier agreement between commercial banks to stop further corporate collapses.
Shares of the Jinro Group's other listed affiliates fell sharply. Jinro Industries was down 420 won to 4,920 and Jinro General Foods was down 360 won to 4,240.

A Chung Won official said it was unable to settle 500-600 million won in promissory notes on Monday and would face a final deadline by the end of Tuesday. Chung Won fell 550 won to its limit-down of 6,330 before trading in its shares was halted.
Chipmaker Samsung Electronics closed down 1,500 won at 60,000. LG Semicon was down 600 won to 26,800. Hyundai Electronics fell 900 won to 36,200.
